                    [32m'        """Wrap a function to create and manage Langfuse tracing around its execution, supporting both synchronous and asynchronous functions.\n'[39m +

                    [32m"        Using OpenTelemetry's distributed tracing system, it maintains proper trace context propagation throughout your application,\n"[39m +
                    [32m'        enabling you to see hierarchical traces of function calls with detailed performance metrics and function-specific details.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        Args:\n'[39m +

                    [32m'                    "generation", "span", "agent", "tool", "chain", "retriever", "embedding", "evaluator", "guardrail".\n'[39m +
                    [32m'                    Observation types are highlighted in the Langfuse UI for filtering and visualization.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'                    The types "generation" and "embedding" create a span on which additional attributes such as model metrics\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'  - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, use a single executeCommand call with \'&&\' to chain them together (e.g., `git add . && git commit -m "message" && git push`).             [32m"  - Use ';' only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail\n"[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Committing changes with git\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Only create commits when requested by the user. If unclear, ask first. When the user asks you to create a new git commit, follow these steps carefully:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Git Safety Protocol:\n'[39m +

Taking unauthorized destructive actions is unhelpful and can result in lost work, so it's best to ONLY run these commands when given direct instructions \n"[39m +

Instead, after hook failure, fix the issue, re-stage, and create a NEW commit\n'[39m +

                    [32m'from langfuse.types import SpanLevel\n'[39m +

                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'class LangfuseObservationWrapper:\n'[39m +

                    [32m'def _detach_context_token_safely(token: Any) -> None:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    """Detach a context token without emitting noisy async teardown errors.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    OpenTelemetry tokens are backed by ``contextvars`` and must be detached in the\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    same execution context where they were attached. Async frameworks can legitimately\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    end spans or unwind context managers in a different task/context, in which case\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    detach raises and the public OpenTelemetry helper logs an error. At that point the\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    observation is already completed, so the mismatch is safe to ignore.\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    """\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    try:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        _RUNTIME_CONTEXT.detach(token)\n'[39m +
                    [32m'    except Exception:\n'[39m +
                    [32m'        pass\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'\n'[39m +
                    [32m'def propagate_attributes(\n'[39m +

                    [32m"    If you call `propagate_attributes` late in your workflow, earlier spans won't be\n"[39m +
